findings.statement: CXCR2, the top-ranked candidate, is almost entirely a neutrophil transcript in inflamed UC mucosa (Gubatan neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). In Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, the small residual signal sits in T/NK and macrophage clusters and the second dataset says myeloid, so the lineage attribution is not replicated. After adjusting for cell composition, the change is only partly retained [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. It is best read as a marker of neutrophil influx, and a CXCR2 antagonist would act on arriving neutrophils rather than on resident tissue cells.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells in Smillie (macrophages, inflammatory monocytes, DC2) and the second dataset agrees, but in Gubatan neutrophils carry most transcripts [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. The composition-adjusted change is no longer significant [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523], verdict composition. Treat it as a marker of myeloid/neutrophil influx; the adjustment may over-correct when resident cells are activated, so this is not proof of pure influx.

IL1B is a myeloid gene (macrophages, inflammatory monocytes, DC2; second dataset agrees) with a large neutrophil contribution in inflamed mucosa [gene=IL1B; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.702]. Its bulk increase does not survive composition adjustment [gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0728], verdict composition, so the bulk rise mostly tracks myeloid influx.

S100A8 is made by macrophages and inflammatory monocytes in Smillie (second dataset concordant) and mostly by neutrophils in Gubatan [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]. A significant part of the change remains after adjustment [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231], verdict partly_composition: a myeloid-influx biomarker with some activation signal.

AQP9 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come overwhelmingly from neutrophils [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]. It retains a smaller positive change after composition adjustment that stays significant [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551], verdict partly_composition. It is a neutrophil-influx marker with no drug in the ranking.

CD274 (PD-L1) is spread across plasma cells, macrophages and enterocytes in Smillie with a modest myeloid lineage share, and neutrophils contribute heavily in Gubatan [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. The change is partly retained after adjustment [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]. The signal is diffuse, so cell-type-specific targeting is unclear; checkpoint agonism rather than blockade would be the direction of interest.

IDO1 is a myeloid gene (DC1, macrophages; second dataset agrees) with an epithelial contribution in Gubatan and little neutrophil contribution [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]. The change is retained after adjustment [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505], verdict partly_composition, so it is a tissue-level change that does not depend on neutrophil influx.

MMP1 is a stromal gene, made chiefly by inflammatory fibroblasts and WNT5B+ fibroblasts, with the second dataset also stromal [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.871]. It keeps a strong change after composition adjustment [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636], so it is a replicated fibroblast-derived tissue change, not neutrophil influx.

CHI3L1 is stromal, concentrated in inflammatory fibroblasts, and the second dataset agrees [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941]. A large change persists after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]. Neutrophils also contribute in Gubatan, so part of the bulk signal is influx, but the fibroblast change is intrinsic.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes and immature enterocytes) and replicated in the second dataset [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]. It retains a clear change after adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161], with almost no neutrophil contribution, so it reflects an epithelial-intrinsic inflammatory program.

In situ, CXCR2 is explained by neutrophils in the deconvolved Visium spots [gene=CXCR2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.386], the composition-corrected source is also neutrophil, and neutrophils are the only cell group enriched around its high spots. In Xenium single cells, inflamed-section attribution is led by neutrophils and neutrophils are the most enriched neighbours of expressing cells (also endothelial cells). This agrees with the Gubatan neutrophil attribution and contradicts the T/NK label in Smillie, which lacks neutrophils. Visium sections with data were few, so this is moderate evidence.

CXCL8 is explained mainly by neutrophils in Visium spots [gene=CXCL8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.609], followed by inflammatory fibroblasts and myeloid cells; the composition-corrected source is myeloid, and neutrophils, inflammatory fibroblasts and myeloid cells are enriched around high spots. Not on the Xenium panel. This agrees with Gubatan (neutrophil-heavy) and partly with Smillie (myeloid), but the fibroblast contribution is not seen at single-cell level.

In Visium spots MMP1 is explained by inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579], the composition-corrected source is also inflammatory fibroblast, and high spots are surrounded by inflammatory fibroblasts and neutrophils. Not on the Xenium panel. This agrees with the stromal single-cell attribution in both datasets; the neutrophil neighbourhood fits the inflamed niche rather than neutrophil production.

In Visium spots the largest raw contributor to CHI3L1 is plasma cells [gene=CHI3L1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.258], but the composition-corrected source is inflammatory fibroblast and inflammatory fibroblasts are the most enriched neighbours of high spots. Not on the Xenium panel. After correction this agrees with the single-cell fibroblast attribution; the plasma signal likely reflects spatial co-location.

DUOX2 is the cleanest in-situ agreement: Visium deconvolution assigns it to epithelial cells [gene=DUOX2; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.812], with epithelial cells also the corrected source and the enriched neighbour. In Xenium single cells the inflamed-section attribution is epithelial and expressing cells are surrounded by epithelium. This matches the epithelial single-cell attribution in both datasets.

In situ IDO1 is ambiguous. Visium deconvolution gives epithelial cells the largest raw share [gene=IDO1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.349], T/NK second, but the composition-corrected source is myeloid. Xenium inflamed-section attribution is led by epithelial cells, with immune cells (T/NK, B, neutrophils, myeloid) enriched among neighbours. This agrees with the myeloid single-cell label only after correction; an epithelial source (also seen in Gubatan) is plausible.

CD274 has no clear in-situ source: Visium deconvolution gives epithelial and neutrophil cells similar shares [gene=CD274; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.234], the composition-corrected source is myeloid, and no cell group is enriched around high spots. It is not on the Xenium panel. This neither confirms nor refutes the diffuse single-cell attribution.

In Visium spots S100A8 is explained by neutrophils [gene=S100A8; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.632], the composition-corrected source is neutrophil, and neutrophils are the most enriched neighbours of high spots, followed by inflammatory fibroblasts and myeloid cells. Not on the Xenium panel. This agrees with the Gubatan neutrophil attribution and with the myeloid lineage in Smillie.

CXCR1 loses most of its bulk change after composition adjustment but stays significant [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.5702], verdict partly_composition. Together with its neutrophil-dominated transcripts it behaves as a neutrophil-influx marker.

CXCL1 retains only a small adjusted change [gene=CXCL1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.3314], verdict partly_composition: mostly cell influx with a minor tissue component.

MMP3 keeps a sizeable change after adjustment [gene=MMP3; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8727], verdict partly_composition, indicating a substantial tissue-intrinsic component.

MMP10 has the largest retained change among the genes checked [gene=MMP10; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.5838], verdict partly_composition, so it is mostly a change inside the tissue rather than cell arrival.

caveats: Composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated, so a lost change (CXCL8, IL1B) is not proof of pure influx.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; Smillie did not capture neutrophils, so neutrophil genes are attributed to other clusters there.
Visium spots hold several cells and only a few UC sections express each gene; deconvolution and spot co-variation are weaker than single-cell evidence. Many genes are not on the Xenium panel.
TREM1 was not assessed individually; it is strongly neutrophil-dominated in Gubatan.
